name: King of Hepher
overview: The King of Hepher was a male monarch known primarily for being one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture, and no additional personal details are provided beyond his role as a defeated king. This title reflects his position as a ruler over the city or region of Hepher during this period.
namesAndTitles: The designation 'King of Hepher' is a title rather than a personal name, directly indicating his rule over Hepher. The meaning is straightforward, identifying him simply as the king associated with that location, as recorded in Joshua 12:17.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for the King of Hepher beyond his identification as a king. There are no recorded relatives or lineage details associated with him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Hepher holds significance as part of the comprehensive list of Canaanite kings defeated by Joshua, marking the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to Israel. His defeat symbolizes the divine empowerment of Israel in their conquest and the establishment of God's chosen people in the Promised Land. Though little personal information is given, his mention underscores the historical reality of Israel's military victories under God's guidance.
